title: Aegis fleet verifier state file (fleet-state.json)
description: What `fleet.py watch` writes after every cycle to STATE_DIR/fleet-state.json (/var/lib/aegis on the gateway, ~/.local/state/aegis for a user on a PC; --state names another file): the verdict of every policy entry in that cycle. Written whole and renamed into place. `fleet.py once` prints the same verdicts as a JSON list. Not signed: the signed statement of a verdict is its attestation result (docs/evidence-format.md). The verdict object is #/$defs/verdict.
$comment: Aegis 1.1 as written (gateway/aegisd/fleet.py attest, credential_step, record_enforcement, issue_result, run_once). 1.2: the verdict's warnings and details also go into the signed result: see docs/data-formats.md once v12-verifier lands.

updated.description: Unix time the file was written

verdicts.description: one per policy entry, in the policy's order

endpoint.description: the policy entry's name ("?" if the entry had none and its attestation raised)

time.description: Unix time the quote was asked for

admitted.description: true exactly when reasons is empty

reasons.description: why it is not admitted; free text for people, not a closed list

evidence_format.description: only for an entry that asks for standard evidence; absent: the older quote (PQ kinds) or a PSA token (kind psa)

elapsed_s.description: seconds from the request to the answer (or to the failure)

pq_signature.description: PQ kinds: the evidence's ML-DSA-65 signature verified with the pinned key

device_pk_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the 1952-byte ML-DSA-65 public key the evidence was verified with

quote.description: the quote as signed, which a session of this cycle continues (transcript v2)

token_sha3_256.description: SHA3-256 of the bytes the device's ML-DSA-65 signature covers: the token (older quote, without the label) or the COSE Sig_structure (EAT)

warning.description: set with an admission the operator must hear about (development key, development profile, unbound session); free text

measurements.description: {measurement_type: measurement_value} as reported: lower-case hex (normally SHA-256) for every component of an admitted verdict; a refused verdict carries what the claims held

instance_id.description: normally a string or null: the claims' instance ID in hex: 0x01 || SHA-256 of the IAK's point (PSA token), 0x02 || SHA-256 of the ML-DSA-65 key (older Aegis claims), the UEID 0x01 || SHA-256 of that key (EAT); null if the claims have none. A refused verdict carries what the claims held.

enforce_rc.description: exit status of the policy's enforce_cmd; null without a hook (or one that did not start or finish)

enforce_error.description: the hook's stderr, with enforcement FAILED

credential.description: for an entry with "provision": what became of its session this cycle; free text

session_binding.description: how a session issued or kept this cycle is tied to the attestation

attestation_result.description: only when the policy asks for results ("attestation_results": true, or the entry's "evidence_format": "eat-cose-v1")

error.description: why no result could be signed; the verdict stands

kind.description: the policy entry's kind (psa when the entry names none). An entry of another kind is refused at the policy stage.

trust.description: closed list; docs/data-formats.md says what each means. Absent for kind psa unless its IAK is TF-M's development key, and for a verdict refused before the claims were read.

enrolment.description: PQ kinds only: how the pinned ML-DSA-65 key came to be trusted. refused: the entry requires an endorsement and the record was refused (never admitted).

endorsement.description: the accepted endorsement record, with enrolment endorsed

endorser_name.description: the policy's name for the endorser key (endorsers[].name), not the record's own

record_sha256.description: the record's name, what endorsement_sha256 pins: JSON form SHA-256 of canonical JSON {"body", "sig"}; COSE form SHA-256 of the file
